we.definition: A word for me and the other people with me.
we.example: Today we are going to the library.

weak.example: The baby bird was too weak to fly yet.

wear.definition: To have clothes or other things on your body.
wear.example: I wear my red boots when it rains.

weather.definition: What it is like outside, such as sunny, rainy or windy.
weather.example: The weather today is warm and sunny.

web.definition: A thin net of silk that a spider spins.
web.example: A spider spun a web in the corner.

week.example: We go swimming once a week.

weeks.definition: Groups of seven days in a row.
weeks.example: Summer camp lasts for two weeks.

weight.example: The nurse checked my weight on a scale.

well.example: She sings well and loves to perform for her family.

went.definition: Moved from one place to another in the past.
went.example: We went to the zoo last Sunday.

were.definition: A word that tells how people or things seemed in the past.
were.example: The puppies were tired after playing.

west.definition: The direction where the sun goes down at night.
west.example: The sun sets in the west each evening.

western.definition: In, from or toward the west.
western.example: We drove to the western side of the lake.

wet.example: My socks got wet in the puddle.

what.definition: A word used to ask about a thing.
what.example: What would you like for lunch today?

when.definition: A word that asks or tells the time something happens.
when.example: When does the movie start tonight?

where.definition: A word that asks or tells about a place.
where.example: Where did you put my red ball?

whereas.definition: But on the other hand; used to show a difference.
whereas.example: My cat is lazy, whereas my dog loves to run.

whether.definition: If; used when there are two choices.
whether.example: I can't decide whether to draw or paint.

which.definition: A word used to ask about one out of a group.
which.example: Which book do you want to read tonight?

while.definition: During the time that something else happens.
while.example: I hummed a song while I painted.

white.definition: The color of fresh snow or milk.
white.example: The bunny had soft white fur.

who.definition: A word used to ask which person.
who.example: Who left their shoes by the door?

whole.definition: All of something, with no part missing.
whole.example: I ate the whole apple, even the skin.

whom.definition: A word for which person, used after words like to or for.
whom.example: To whom did you give the flowers?

whose.definition: A word that asks or tells which person something belongs to.
whose.example: Whose red jacket is on the floor?

why.definition: A word used to ask for the reason.
why.example: Why is the sky so blue today?

wide.definition: Big from one side to the other.
wide.example: The river is wide and slow.

widely.definition: In many places or by lots of people.
widely.example: Soccer is widely played all over the world.

widespread.definition: Found in many places or among many people.
widespread.example: There was widespread joy when the snow day was announced.

wife.definition: A married woman; the woman someone is married to.
wife.example: Uncle Joe and his wife baked us a pie.

wild.definition: Living free in nature, not kept by people.
wild.example: We saw wild deer near the forest path.

will.definition: A word that tells about something that is going to happen.
will.example: Tomorrow we will plant seeds in the garden.

win.definition: To come in first in a game or race.
win.example: I hope our team can win the game.

wind.definition: Air moving outside that you can feel blowing.
wind.example: The wind blew my hat off my head.

window.definition: An opening in a wall with glass that lets in light.
window.example: I looked out the window at the falling snow.

windows.definition: Openings in walls with glass that let in light and air.
windows.example: We washed all the windows until they sparkled.

wing.definition: A part of a bird or bug used for flying.
wing.example: The bird flapped one wing and then the other.

winning.definition: Coming out on top in a game or race.
winning.example: Our team is ahead and winning by two points.

wins.definition: Comes in first in a game or race.
wins.example: My brother always wins at checkers.

winter.definition: The coldest time of the year.
winter.example: In winter we build snowmen in the yard.

wire.definition: A long, thin, bendy piece of metal.
wire.example: Dad used wire to fix the garden fence.

wish.definition: To hope for something you would like.
wish.example: I wish it would snow tomorrow.

with.definition: Alongside or in the company of someone or something.
with.example: I went to the park with my sister.

within.example: The toys are kept within the big wooden box.

without.example: I can't sleep without my teddy bear.

wolf.definition: A wild animal like a big dog that lives in a pack.
wolf.example: We heard a wolf howl at the moon.

woman.definition: A grown-up female person; a lady.
woman.example: The woman at the library helped me find a book.

women.definition: Grown-up female people; more than one lady.
women.example: Two women were walking their dogs in the park.

won.definition: Came in first in a game or contest.
won.example: Our class won the reading prize this year.

wood.definition: The hard stuff that trees are made of.
wood.example: Grandpa built a birdhouse out of wood.

word.definition: A group of letters that has a meaning when you say or read it.
word.example: Cat is the first word I learned to read.

words.definition: Groups of letters that each mean something.
words.example: I can read all the words in this book.

wore.definition: Had clothes or things on your body in the past.
wore.example: She wore a yellow dress to the party.

work.definition: To do a job or task that takes effort.
work.example: Mom and Dad work hard every day.

worked.definition: Did a job or task that took effort.
worked.example: Grandma worked in her garden until sunset.

workers.definition: People who have a job and do it.
workers.example: The workers built a new bridge over the river.

working.definition: Doing a job or task that takes effort.
working.example: The bees are busy working in the hive.

works.definition: Does a job or task that takes effort.
works.example: My aunt works at the animal shelter.

world.definition: The Earth and all the people, places and things on it.
world.example: There are many animals all over the world.

worldwide.definition: Found or happening all over the Earth.
worldwide.example: The game is played by children worldwide.

worm.definition: A small, long, soft animal with no legs that lives in soil.
worm.example: The robin pulled a worm out of the grass.

worn.definition: Had on the body, like clothes or shoes.
worn.example: These boots have been worn every winter.

would.definition: A word used to talk about what might happen, or to ask nicely.
would.example: Would you like some more juice?

write.definition: To put letters or words down on paper with a pencil or pen.
write.example: I can write my name in big letters.

writer.definition: A person whose job is making books or stories.
writer.example: The writer read her new book to our class.

writers.definition: People whose job is making books, stories or articles.
writers.example: Many writers visit our school library each year.

writes.definition: Puts letters or words on paper.
writes.example: My brother writes his name very neatly.

writing.definition: Making up stories, poems or books with words.
writing.example: She is writing a story about a magic dragon.

writings.definition: Stories, poems or letters that someone has made.
writings.example: We read the writings of a famous poet in class.

written.definition: Made up as a story, poem or book.
written.example: This book was written by my favorite author.

wrote.definition: Put letters or words on paper in the past.
wrote.example: I wrote a story about a brave little mouse.

yacht.definition: A fancy boat with sails or a motor, used for trips or races.
yacht.example: A shiny white yacht sailed into the harbor.

yards.definition: Grassy spaces next to houses where you can play.
yards.example: Kids played tag in their front yards all afternoon.

year.definition: A span of twelve months, or 365 days.
year.example: My birthday comes once a year.

years.example: My sister is seven years old.

yellow.definition: The color of a banana or the bright sun.
yellow.example: She painted the sun bright yellow.

yet.example: The bus has not come yet.

you.definition: A word for the person someone is talking to.
you.example: Thank you for the lovely gift.

young.definition: Not old; in the early part of life.
young.example: The young puppy rolled in the soft green grass.

younger.definition: Having lived fewer years than someone else.
younger.example: My younger sister is learning to ride her bike.

your.definition: Belonging to the person you are talking to.
your.example: Please put your shoes by the front door.

zephyr.definition: A soft, gentle wind that feels cool and fresh.
zephyr.example: The kite floated up on a gentle zephyr by the sea.

zero.definition: The number that means none at all, written as 0.
zero.example: If you eat all three cookies, you will have zero left.

zone.definition: An area that is set apart for something special.
zone.example: The playground has a quiet zone for reading books.

zoo.definition: A park where people can visit and see wild animals.
zoo.example: We saw a tall giraffe eating leaves at the zoo.
